rationale: Compound ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲍⲁⲩⲧ (root unidentified). In context (the body-region from heart down to thighs, mapped to 'this earth' below the air) functions as the body's earthly/lower zone. Possibly related to ⲍⲁⲩ 'bitter/lower' or to a dwelling/staying verb. Confidence low.

Plural noun in the cosmic-architectural inventory of line 19 (firmaments / hosts / ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲉ / preparations / strongholds). Etymology unclear; possibly cognate with ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise' giving 'risings/ascents' or with a watch/post-noun. Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestations.

Likely orthographic variant of ⲡⲉϩⲍⲏⲡⲁⲣ 'his liver' (Greek ἧπαρ, already in accumulated vocabulary), with ⲧ for expected ⲡ. Either a scribal slip or a Lycopolitan dialectal variant. Body-mapping context (liver → fire-stronghold, paralleled by flesh → darkness-stronghold, sinew → water-stronghold) confirms anatomical reading.

Body part falling between knees (ⲛⲉϩⲕⲉⲍⲧⲉ) and feet/soles in the descending mapping. Likely related to accumulated tentative ⲛⲉⲩⲥⲛⲩⲉ 'their legs (tentative).' The ϩ-form may be a singular/possessed variant of the same root.

Lyc. variant of ⲛⲁϭ/ⲛⲁⲟ/ⲛⲁⲃ 'great' as title-prefix. Confirmed by the standard Manichaean cosmological title 'Great King of Honor' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲛⲁⲃ ⲛⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ⲛⲧⲉ ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲟ). The chain of dialectal variants ⲛⲁϭ→ⲛⲁⲃ→ⲛⲁⲟ→ⲛⲁⲩ is plausible.

Likely Lycopolitan orthographic variant of standard ⲙⲙⲁⲩ 'there' with epenthetic/dialectal ϩ for ⲩ. Functions as a discourse-locative closing the description of each watch's authority-zone (lines 26, 30). Distinct from homograph ⲙⲁϩ 'fill' or ordinal-prefix ⲙⲁϩ-.
